# Pinterest Marketing for Small Business: Is It Worth Your Time?

Pinterest is a search engine for ideas people are about to act on. For the right small business it quietly drives sales — here is who it works for and how to use it.

[← Back to Blog](https://outcomedigitalmarketing.com/blog)

Written by [Craig Fearn](https://outcomedigitalmarketing.com/about)

Director

Last updated: 9 July 2026

Part of our complete guide: [Digital Marketing in Cornwall: A Practical Guide for Local Businesses](https://outcomedigitalmarketing.com/blog/digital-marketing-cornwall)

**Pinterest is a visual search engine for things people are about to plan or buy.** Unlike Instagram or Facebook, people do not go to Pinterest to catch up with friends — they go to find ideas: a kitchen they want to build, a wedding they are planning, a recipe for Friday. That planning mindset is what makes it work for some small businesses and do nothing for others. This guide covers who Pinterest actually works for, why its buying intent is different, and how to use it without wasting time.

TL;DR

Pinterest is a search engine for ideas, not a social feed — people use it to plan purchases, so the buying intent is high and pins last for months, not days. It works for visual, planning-led businesses: interiors, weddings, food, fashion, crafts, home improvement, travel. It is a poor fit if you have nothing visual to show. Post a few quality pins a week that link back to your [website](https://outcomedigitalmarketing.com/website-design-cornwall), and let them accumulate. It complements search and your [other channels](https://outcomedigitalmarketing.com/digital-marketing-cornwall) rather than replacing them.

## Why Pinterest Is Not Really Social Media

The mistake most businesses make is treating Pinterest like Instagram. It is closer to Google. People arrive with a search in mind — “small kitchen ideas”, “coastal wedding”, “Cornwall self-catering” — and Pinterest shows them images that link to pages where they can learn more or buy. The intent is different, and so is the shelf life. A strong pin keeps surfacing in search and bringing clicks for months or even years, long after an Instagram post has vanished from the feed.

Pinterest reached **631 million monthly active users globally in early 2026, up 11% year on year** ([Pinterest Q1 2026 results](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260504431866/en/Pinterest-Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Results)), including around **15.5 million in the UK — roughly 22% of the population** ([DataReportal, 2025](https://datareportal.com/essential-pinterest-stats)). And **96% of top searches on Pinterest are unbranded** ([Pinterest Business](https://business.pinterest.com/audience/)) — people are looking for ideas, not a brand they already know, which is exactly the gap a small business can fill.

## Does It Actually Drive Sales?

Plenty of social platforms generate attention without generating a penny of revenue. Pinterest’s edge is that its users are often already in a buying frame of mind.

A UK study using Tesco Clubcard purchase data found that shoppers exposed to Pinterest **spent 26% more over a year, visited stores 25% more often, and had a spend-per-converted-customer around eight times higher than other UK social platforms** ([Pinterest / Dunnhumby, 2025](https://business.pinterest.com/en-gb/blog/liveramp-study-pinterest-sales-lift/)). Around **80% of weekly users say they feel inspired to shop** by the platform ([Pinterest Business](https://business.pinterest.com/audience/)).

That does not make Pinterest a fit for everyone. It skews towards planning-led, visual purchases, and in the UK the audience skews female — around **71% of UK users** ([Statista, 2025](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1014153/pinterest-users-in-the-united-kingdom-uk-by-gender/)) — though its fastest-growing group globally is now Gen Z. If your customers and your product line up with that, the intent is genuinely there.

## Who Pinterest Works For

Think about whether your business is something people **plan**. It works well for interiors, weddings, food, fashion, crafts, holiday lets, and anything design-led. A Cornwall holiday let, a wedding photographer, a furniture maker, or a café with photogenic food all have a natural home here. If your business is none of those — a plumber, an accountant, a B2B service — your time is almost certainly better spent on [local SEO](https://outcomedigitalmarketing.com/seo-cornwall) and Google.

## How to Use It Without Wasting Time

Every pin should be a genuinely useful image that links back to a relevant page on your own website — a product, a guide, a booking page — so the traffic goes somewhere you own and can convert. Write clear, keyword-led descriptions so pins get found in Pinterest’s search. Post a few quality pins a week rather than a daily flood, and let them build up; the long shelf life does the compounding for you.

Pinterest is rarely a business’s main channel, and it shouldn’t be. But for the right visual, planning-led business it’s a quiet, durable source of high-intent traffic that most competitors overlook. Not sure it fits your Cornwall business? Ask us — the [digital marketing](https://outcomedigitalmarketing.com/digital-marketing-cornwall) we do starts with working out which channels earn their place and which don’t.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Is Pinterest good for small businesses?

For the right kind of business, yes. Pinterest works best when your product or service is visual and tied to planning — weddings, interiors, food, fashion, crafts, home improvement, travel, and events. People use Pinterest to plan things they intend to do or buy, so a business that helps them do that gets found at exactly the right moment. It is a weaker fit for businesses with nothing visual to show.

How is Pinterest different from Instagram or Facebook?

Pinterest is really a visual search engine, not a social feed. People come to it looking for ideas and planning purchases, rather than to chat with friends. That means the intent is higher and the content lasts far longer — a good pin can keep bringing traffic for months or years, whereas an Instagram post is mostly forgotten within days. It rewards useful, well-organised content over frequent posting.

Many Americans use social media to connect with one another, engage with news content, share information and entertain themselves. Explore the patterns and trends shaping the social media landscape.

About this research

This fact sheet is the latest in our long-running series on technology adoption in the United States. For more than a decade, we’ve surveyed Americans to understand which social media platforms they use.

#### Why did we do this?

Pew Research Center does research to inform the public, journalists and decision-makers. This research builds on our past work [studying social media platforms Americans use](https://www.pewresearch.org/topic/internet-technology/platforms-services/social-media/).

[Learn more about Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/about/).

#### [](https://www.pewresearch.org/topic/internet-technology/platforms-services/social-media/)How did we do this?

This analysis is based on findings from the National Public Opinion Reference Survey, a Center survey of 5,511 U.S. adults. We allowed people to respond online, by mail or by phone. The survey represents the views of all U.S. adults.

The survey was conducted Jan. 30-June 18, 2026. Its overall margin of error is plus or minus 1.8 percentage points.

This analysis also includes past data. The ways we’ve allowed people to respond to these surveys have evolved over the years, including in 2023 and again in 2024. For more on these shifts and how we approached them, read our [mobile](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/mobile/) and [broadband](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/internet-broadband/) fact sheets and [our Q&A](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2024/01/31/q-and-a-how-and-why-were-changing-the-way-we-study-tech-adoption/).

Here are the [questions used for this analysis](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/10/PI_2026.10.19_NPORS-Internet-Fact-Sheets_Questionnaire.pdf), the [topline](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/10/PI_2026.10.19_NPORS-Internet-Fact-Sheets_TOPLINE.pdf) and the [survey methodology](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/10/PI_2026.10.19_NPORS-Internet-Fact-Sheets_Methodology.pdf).

# About A/B testing for Meta Ads

A/B testing enables you to compare two versions of an ad strategy by changing variables such as ad images, ad text, audience or placement. Each version is shown to a segment of your audience, ensuring nobody sees both, then the test determines which version performs best. Running an A/B test helps you decide which ad strategy to use.

Before you select a variable to test, choose a [hypothesis for your test](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2358258211160819). For example, you might hypothesize that a custom audience strategy will outperform an interest-based audience strategy for your business.

## How A/B testing works in Meta Ads Manager

To create an A/B test, you can either duplicate an existing campaign, ad set or ad and change a variable, or compare two existing campaigns or ad sets. If you choose to duplicate an existing campaign, your ad budget is also duplicated. Otherwise, your current ad budgets are used, which you can change in Meta Ads Manager at the ad set level. Use the same budget for both versions in a test to ensure a fair comparison. A/B testing can then measure the performance of each strategy on a cost per result basis or cost per conversion lift basis.

## When to use an A/B test for your Meta ads

We recommend A/B testing when you’re trying to measure changes to your advertising or quickly compare two strategies. We do not recommend testing informally, such as by turning ad sets or campaigns on and off manually. Informal testing can lead to inefficient ad delivery and unreliable test results. For example, A/B testing helps ensure your audiences will be evenly split and statistically comparable, while informal testing can lead to overlapping audiences.

You can [create an A/B test in Meta Ads Manager](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/355670925639619) or in the [**Experiments** tool](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/3506622486044209). Learn more about the [ways to create an A/B test](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1159714227408868).
